summary: Wilkes County state educational forest tower; NHLR dates it to 1936, a 1934-36 state report describes a different steel tower; no longer used and unsafe to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives a 50-foot Aermotor tower (about 15.2 m). The 1934-36 state report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives a 59-foot-3-inch steel tower (about 18.1 m). These may be different structures, so height is left out of facts until resolved.

The 1934-36 state report quoted by Forest Lookouts says the CCC erected a steel tower in October 1934. NHLR and the Journal-Patriot give 1936. Both dates are recorded as events; the record's 1936 is kept as the build date.

notes_for_editor: The 18 m height in the brief matches the 1934-36 state report's 59 ft 3 in steel tower, not the NHLR's 50 ft Aermotor (15.2 m), so height_m is left out of facts. The record's 1936 build year is from NHLR and the Journal-Patriot; the 1934 report is quoted second-hand by Forest Lookouts and was not checked against the original. The Journal-Patriot article is partly paywalled, but the quoted lines were readable and the article's own date is not shown. The Wilkes Record column is dated December 10, 2023. A TV item quoting a ranger on a 1936 CCC build was not fetched and is not cited. NHLR's 'restricted for electronics use' is quoted as written; no source explains what it means. Access is set to restricted because the tower is described as unsafe to climb; no official closure notice was found. Staffing is recorded as unstaffed on the strength of the undated Journal-Patriot report.
